transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I’ve been feeling like the best part of my life is behind me. Not in a dramatic way, just… quietly, but it doesn’t seem to go away. I’ve always thought if I planned well and stayed disciplined I could get myself back on track, but lately it feels like none of that is getting me back to feeling like myself.
How long have you been feeling like the best part of your life is behind you?
It started after my hiking injury, a little over three years ago. So… about three years and three months now.
Do you find yourself enjoying activities that you used to find pleasurable?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I still do some things I used to like, but I don’t know that I’ve paid close attention to whether I’m enjoying them the same way. It’s not an easy yes or no for me.
Do you feel like you've been taking pleasure in the things you're doing lately?
I’m not sure. I think I still go through the motions with things, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m actually taking pleasure in them. It’s hard for me to say clearly.
Have you noticed any change in how much pleasure you get from things you used to enjoy?
I honestly haven’t been tracking it closely. I still do some of the same things, but I can’t say for sure whether the pleasure is less or just… different. I’m not really sure.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?
I’m not really sure I’d say I’ve lost interest. I still do some of the things I used to enjoy. I just haven’t thought much about whether my interest has really changed.
Do you feel sad most of the time?

Most days, yes, there’s a sadness there. I’m not in tears all the time or anything like that, but there’s this low, gray feeling underneath things, even when I’m doing normal stuff like being in the studio or having dinner with my wife.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that normally would bring you happiness?
I’m not sure I’d put it that strongly. I can still enjoy things at times, I think. It’s more that I haven’t really paid close attention to whether I’m feeling pleasure the way I used to.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight recently?
I haven’t really noticed any significant change, no. My weight seems about the same as far as I can tell.
Do you feel like this sadness has been with you nearly every day since your injury?
Yes. It’s been there pretty much since the hiking injury—so, a little over three years now. About three years and three months, I guess.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that normally would bring you happiness?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’m completely unable to enjoy things, but I haven’t paid enough attention to know if it’s changed much.
Are there things that you used to enjoy doing, but now you don't enjoy them as much?
I’m not sure, honestly. I still do some of the things I used to like, but I haven’t really noticed clearly whether I enjoy them less or not. It’s kind of hard for me to tell.
Do you feel like things that used to give you pleasure no longer do?
I don’t really know. I can’t say for sure that they no longer give me pleasure. I still do some things, but I haven’t really paid close attention to whether the enjoyment is different.
Have you had any periods of two months or more where you didn't feel this sadness?

No, not really. It’s not like I’m crying every day or anything dramatic, but most days there’s just this low, gray feeling underneath things. Even if I’m in the studio or having dinner with my wife, it’s kind of still there.
Do you feel like things that normally would bring you happiness no longer give you any pleasure at all?

I wouldn’t say no pleasure at all. That feels too strong. I can’t really tell that clearly—some things still feel okay, maybe just not as much as I’d expect. But I haven’t really been tracking it closely.
Have you had any periods where you felt completely back to normal for at least two months since your injury?
No, I don’t think so. Since the hiking injury, it’s pretty much been there the whole time. That was a little over three years ago—about three years and three months now.
Do you feel like you're unable to find pleasure in almost all activities?
I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I still get some enjoyment from things here and there. It’s just… kind of muted sometimes, not gone across the board.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed most of the day?

Yes, I think so. Most days I’m not crying or anything dramatic, but there’s this low, gray feeling underneath things for a lot of the day. Even when I’m in the studio or having dinner with my wife, it’s kind of there in the background.
Have you had any periods where you felt completely back to normal for more than two months at a time since your injury?

No, not really. Like I said, it’s been going on since that hiking injury—just over three years now, about three years and three months. I haven’t had a stretch that long where I felt completely back to normal.
Have you had periods of less than two months where you didn't feel this sadness?
Maybe short stretches, yes, but not anything that lasted. Since the hiking injury a little over three years ago—about three years and three months now—it’s mostly just been there in some form.
